clause-1-scope.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 1 describes what the standard covers: accessibility requirements for ICT products and services, together with the test procedures and evaluation methodology that go with them.

clause-2-references.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 2 lists the documents this standard refers to. It is split into normative references, which are necessary for applying the standard, and informative references, which provide background and context.

clause-3-definitions.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 3 defines the terms and abbreviations used throughout the standard. Use the A to Z index at the start of each list to jump straight to a definition.

clause-4-functional-performance.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 4 sets out the functional performance criteria used throughout the standard. These describe what people need to be able to do — for example, see, hear or operate a control — rather than how a product must be built. Later clauses refer back to these criteria.

clause-5-generic-requirements.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 5 contains requirements that apply across many kinds of ICT. It covers closed functionality (where a product prevents people from attaching or using their own assistive technology), activation of accessibility features, biometrics, tactile controls, and locking or toggle controls.

clause-6-real-time-communication.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 6 covers ICT that provides real-time two-way communication. It includes requirements for voice communication, Real-Time Text (RTT), caller ID, alternatives to voice-based services, and video communication.

clause-7-video-capabilities.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 7 covers ICT that plays video with synchronised audio. It sets out requirements for subtitle processing, audio description, and user control of these accessibility features.

clause-8-hardware.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 8 covers physical products, including their controls, displays and connectors. It sets out what makes hardware accessible to use.

clause-9-web.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 9 applies Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 requirements to web pages.

clause-10-non-web-documents.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 10 covers documents that are not web pages, such as PDF or word-processed files. It sets out what makes these documents accessible.

clause-11-non-web-software.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 11 covers software that is not a web page, such as desktop or mobile applications. It sets out what makes this software accessible.

clause-12-information-products-services.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 12 covers the information provided with a product or service — including documentation of its accessibility and compatibility features — and electronic program guides.

clause-13-relay-emergency.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 13 covers access to relay services, which convert between modes of communication such as text and speech, and includes informative material on access to emergency services.

clause-14-conformance.heading: About this clause
text: Clause 14 explains what it means for a product or service to conform with this standard, and how conformance is assessed.

annex-a-conformance-evaluation.heading: About this annex
text: Annex A supports evaluating whether a specific product or service meets the essential requirements of the EU accessibility directives covered by this standard. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-b-functional-performance-relations.heading: About this annex
text: Annex B shows which requirements in clauses 5 to 13 support each of the functional performance criteria in clause 4. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-c-1-introduction.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C describes ways to determine whether individual requirements are met. It is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-4-functional-performance.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.4 describes how meeting the functional performance criteria in clause 4 is assessed. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-5-generic-requirements.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.5 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 5 (generic requirements) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-6-real-time-communication.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.6 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 6 (real-time communication) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-7-video-capabilities.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.7 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 7 (ICT with video capabilities) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-8-hardware.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.8 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 8 (hardware) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-9-web.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.9 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 9 (web) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-10-non-web-documents.heading: About this annex

text: Annex C.11 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 11 (non-web software) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

text: Annex C.12 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 12 (information about products and services) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-13-relay-emergency.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.13 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 13 (relay and emergency service access) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-c-14-conformance.heading: About this annex
text: Annex C.14 describes ways to determine whether the requirements in clause 14 (conformance) are met. Like all of Annex C it is {{normative}}, which means it forms part of the requirements of the standard.

annex-d-cognitive-accessibility.heading: About this annex
text: Annex D points to further resources and guidelines for making ICT accessible to people with limited cognitive, language and learning abilities. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-e-guidance.heading: About this annex
text: Annex E explains how to use the standard: what each clause covers, how to work out which requirements apply to a specific product or service, and where to start. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-za-directive-2016-2102.heading: About this annex
text: Annex ZA sets out how this standard relates to the essential requirements of the Web Accessibility Directive (Directive (EU) 2016/2102), for websites and for mobile applications. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-zb-directive-2019-882.heading: About this annex
text: Annex ZB sets out how this standard relates to the essential requirements of the European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882). It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-zc-other-directives.heading: About this annex
text: Annex ZC sets out how this standard relates to the essential requirements of other Directives, according to Directive (EU) 2019/882, Section VI of Annex I. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.

annex-f-change-history.heading: About this annex
text: Annex F records the history of changes made between versions of this standard. It is {{informative}}, which means it provides guidance rather than setting new requirements.
